clue.text: Shady spots where telephones will lose signal, ultimately

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped from the word, so a letter comes out

parts.note: blower is British slang for a telephone, so telephones are blowers

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word signal

explanation.surface: Somewhere telephones get no reception, perhaps under the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blower' is British slang for a phone. 'Will lose' takes away the L that 'ultimately' picks from the end of 'signal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arbours or leafy garden shelters give shade.

clue.text: Bet on others for support

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Wager on the remaining runners to back you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A backrest is the part of a seat that supports your back.

clue.text: Rumour, some might say, went round fast

indicators.note: some might say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds similar

parts.note: word, as in word has it, is rumour or news

explanation.surface: Gossip, according to some, spread quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'went round fast' as gossip spreading; it means spun round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that spun rapidly with a buzzing noise did so.

clue.text: Manage a session on small cars

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a bout is a spell or session of activity
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Organise a meeting about little cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: runabouts are small light cars for short trips.

clue.text: Coast road company runs cosy little place

parts.note: R stands for runs on a cricket scorecard
a niche is a snug recess or comfortable position

explanation.surface: A firm operates a snug little spot along the seaside drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coastline.

clue.text: Sooner or later, defy senate and shoo out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Eventually you will defy the senate and chase it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' only joins; DEFY, SENATE and SHOO together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an expression meaning at some unspecified future time.

clue.text: Free article turned up low point

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters read upward, so backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A free item turned up at the lowest moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads RIDAN from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the lowest point of fortunes or of the sky beneath an observer.

clue.text: Host with time for right contest

indicators.note: time for right means time takes the place of right

parts.note: a compere hosts a show

explanation.surface: A host with time to fight a right-wing contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to contest is to vie or compete.

clue.text: Players at Zurich admitting substitute

indicators.note: the phrase admits, or contains, the run of letters needed

explanation.surface: Football players in Zurich bring in a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' looks like a sports noun but works as an adjective sense: imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ersatz product is an inferior substitute or imitation.

clue.text: Never worried, accepting trade union with excellent source of finance

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside
worried suggests the letters of never are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: capital is an old-fashioned word for excellent

explanation.surface: Never anxious, welcoming the union with a superb funding source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' makes VENRE, and 'capital' as excellent is a dated British usage, as in 'a capital idea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Venture capital is money invested in new or risky businesses.

clue.text: Customers needing most of nicely polished box

indicators.note: polished suggests the letters are worked over and rearranged
most of a word means it is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: the box and the tele are both informal words for television

explanation.surface: Customers want a nicely finished case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims 'nicely' to NICEL, which 'polished' rearranges to CLIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a clientele is the body of a business's regular customers.

clue.text: Murphy's back around the first of March for deposits

indicators.note: around says one piece is wrapped about the other
back says the word for potato is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a murphy is slang for a potato, also called a spud

indicators.note: the first of picks the opening letter of March

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy returns around early March to make some deposits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns SPUD into DUPS, which goes 'around' the M from 'the first of March'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to put something down heavily is to drop or set it down carelessly.

clue.text: Rodent eating unusual brie dish

indicators.note: eating means one piece swallows the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of brie are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A rat nibbles some odd brie in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges BRIE to REBI, which RAT is 'eating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted cheese on toast.

clue.text: Sacrifice one during poor effort

indicators.note: during puts one thing within the span of another, so it goes inside
poor indicates the word effort is in bad shape, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A weak attempt costs you a single sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges EFFORT to FORFET, with the I 'during' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sacrifice something is to give it up or lose it as a penalty.

clue.text: Unhappy hour, oddly for a holy man

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and other odd-placed letters of hour

explanation.surface: An hour of misery for a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic or wandering holy man in India.

clue.text: Finds new quarters for American welcomed among freed heroes

indicators.note: being welcomed among others means going inside the group
freed suggests the letters of heroes are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: An American is greeted by released hostages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freed' rearranges HEROES to REHOES; US is 'welcomed among' them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to provide someone with new accommodation is to give them a new home.

clue.text: Plain rude — and no different

indicators.note: different suggests the letters take a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Bluntly rude and no change at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plain means without decoration or ornament.

clue.text: Some in action did a runner

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
some is part of a whole

explanation.surface: Taking part in an action, someone fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did a runner' is British slang for leaving in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to do a runner is to leave hastily, often without paying.

clue.text: Vestments needing most of money, then footwear

indicators.note: most of a word means cutting it short by its final letter

parts.note: cash is money
socks are worn on the feet

explanation.surface: Clergy clothing costs most of your cash and then some footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cassock is a long garment worn by clergy and choristers.

clue.text: Money up front for amorous approach

definitions.meaning: a payment made before it is due, such as part of a salary
a romantic or sexual overture to someone

explanation.surface: Pay up front for a romantic overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a loan before payday and an approach made to someone.

clue.text: Popular guest admitting row

indicators.note: the words popular guest admit, or contain, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A well-liked visitor owns up to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' looks like confessing, but it means the words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to row, rhyming with cow, is to quarrel.

clue.text: Appeal of girl disheartened with love affair

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, leaving only the first and last letters of girl

parts.note: an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: The attraction of a dejected girl in a romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: glamour is alluring charm or attractiveness.

clue.text: People count!

parts.note: the surface is a slogan that people matter; read as noun-plus-noun it is an official count of the population

explanation.surface: A rallying cry that people matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An official count of the inhabitants of a country is literally a count of people.

clue.text: Wrap English novel, working quietly

indicators.note: working suggests the word novel is being worked on and rearranged

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: An English novelist wraps up their book, working quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to envelop something is to enclose or cover it completely.

clue.text: Absurdly rich, bagging poem

indicators.note: bagging means holding, so the two words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Ridiculously wealthy, scooping up a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling.

clue.text: Picture designer with a master's degree

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A painting by a fashion designer who holds a master's degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene or model picture, often in a museum.

clue.text: Fly high across pole with echo-sounder

indicators.note: across means one piece stretches over the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: Flying high over the pole with echo-location gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sonar finds objects underwater by bouncing sound pulses off them.

clue.text: Testing toy Turing designed

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are put into a newly planned arrangement

explanation.surface: Alan Turing invented a toy, which is now under test.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: experimenting with something to see if it works is putting it to the test.

clue.text: Check mobile phone? It's a little thing but capable of development

definitions.text: a little thing but capable of development

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check or halt it
a cell is a mobile phone, short for cellphone

explanation.surface: Checking your phone, a small device that might grow into something bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: A stem cell is a tiny unspecialised cell able to develop into many kinds of cell.

clue.text: Much loved mineral, in total

indicators.note: in places the mineral inside the word for total

parts.note: to add up is to total
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A cherished mineral, altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone deeply cherished is greatly loved.
